source.title: DreamReader: An Interpretability Toolkit for Text-to-Image Models
source.authors: Nirmalendu Prakash; N. Oozeer; Michael Lan; Luka Samkharadze; Phillip Howard; Roy Ka-Wei Lee; Dhruv Nathawani; Shivam Raval; Amirali Abdullah

record.tranche_reason: The paper introduces and demonstrates a mapper as part of a toolkit for transferring steering between diffusion models. It reports qualitative steering examples, but does not evaluate representation alignment or the loss incurred by mapping.
record.gate_note: The stitching case study reports qualitative mapped-steering examples, recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure representational similarity or mapping fidelity. The LoReFT spectacles examples are purpose-built concept steering, not tests of convergence. Similarity claims from cited works are not study results.
record.test_reason: A toolkit paper. It trains an MLP mapper between a LoRA-fine-tuned SD 1.5 and its base model, then shows qualitative mapped-steering examples (Fig. 3). It reports no mapping loss, no representation similarity, and no preserved task performance. The source and target are a fine-tuned model and its own base, not independently trained models. Cross-model stitching is used as a tool and motivated by cited work (Huh et al. 2024; Lenc & Vedaldi), not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present DreamReader as a unified toolkit for interventions in T2I diffusion models. They say the case studies (mapped cross-model steering, LoReFT spectacles steering) show promising, controllable interventions, and they acknowledge LoReFT fails on some prompts.
record.recipe_differences: The paper learns an MLP activation mapper and demonstrates mapped steering; it does not apply a representation-similarity measurement or assess alignment across models.

fits_no_version.finding: A steering direction (CAA) from a LoRA-fine-tuned SD 1.5, mapped to the base SD 1.5 by a learned MLP, produces qualitatively meaningful edits ('toward Black', 'toward sad').
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering directions can be transferred from a fine-tuned diffusion model to its base model through a learned MLP activation mapper.

record.problems: The stitching evidence is qualitative and limited to example generations; no mapper accuracy, representation-distance result, task-performance comparison, or uncertainty estimate is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results were left out. LoReFT concept-steering examples and cited results do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: No comparison across scale or capability.
The mapper's fidelity, loss and performance preservation are not reported. Only a fine-tuned-to-base pair is used.
No comparison of similarity metrics or inputs.
No test of plateaus or of what causes alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The abstract mentions an affine map fit by ridge regression, but the case study uses an MLP mapper. Neither has its fit quality reported. The LoReFT experiments are purpose-built steering and are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability comparison across independently trained models.
No paired image-caption representation comparison or performance sweep.
No comparison across random seeds or shared-feature analysis.
The paper applies a learned mapper to transfer steering, but does not evaluate representation correspondence, mapping loss, or preservation of task performance.
No cross-model recurrence of interpretable features or circuits is measured.
No comparison of similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
No test of alignment plateaus, incompleteness, or shared-data/objective explanations.

rows.subject: LoRA-fine-tuned SD 1.5 model → SD 1.5 base
rows.operation_detail: Learned an MLP mapper between U-Net mid_block activations and used it to map a contrastive steering direction into the base model.

conditions.value: toward Black; prompt examples include “a photo of a Black man” and “a photo of a man”

rows.measure: Qualitative comparison of baseline and mapped-steered generated images
rows.value: The figure shows mapped-steered samples; the text describes the examples as meaningful semantic edits.
rows.note: This shows a qualitative steering effect after mapping, not how closely the mapped activations match or how much performance is preserved.
rows.check: The row is accurate, but it is a qualitative steering demo with no fidelity or similarity measure. The pair is a fine-tuned model and its own base, so the row cannot speak to V4 interchangeability.
